title: Bubbly Hands
blurb: Ela gets muddy hands playing in the garden with her dog Paws. As she reaches for Grandpa's watermelon she suddenly stops: first water, then bubbles!

pages.text: Ela and her dog Paws played ball in the garden. Hop, hop, hop! The ball fell in the mud. Splat! Ela grabbed the ball. Paws jumped for joy: “Woof woof!”
pages.ask: What do you like playing most in the garden?

pages.text: Grandpa put watermelon on the table: “Watermelon's ready!” Ela's tummy rumbled: grumble grumble! She reached out her hand at once. Paws reached out his paw too!
pages.ask: What do you do when you're hungry?

pages.text: Ela stopped. She was surprised! She looked at her hands: mud, mud! Sticky, sticky! Paws looked at his paws too. Ela thought: “Hmm… Can I eat watermelon with these hands?”

dede.say: The watermelon won't run away, Ela!

predict.q: What do you think Ela's hands need?
predict.res: They need both! But which one first? Let's see.

pages.ask: Why do you think Ela stopped?

pages.text: Ela went to the bathroom. Paws came pitter-patter behind her. First, water: splish splash! Then, soap: bubbles, bubbles! Rub, rub, rub: one, two, three, four, five… all the way to twenty!
pages.ask: What do you do first when you wash your hands?

pages.text: Ela rinsed her hands. Splish splash! The bubbles and the mud slid away. Click! She turned off the tap. Paws brought the towel. Pat pat, hands all dry!

mech.done: Click! Pat pat! Hands all dry!

pages.ask: Why do you think Ela turned off the tap?

pages.text: Ela sniffed her hands. Mmm, so fresh! She ate watermelon with Grandpa. Then Paws held out his paw. Ela giggled: tee-hee! “Let's wipe your paws first, Paws!”
pages.ask: When do you wash your hands?

kazanim: HSAB.10 (unverified) · Paying attention to cleanliness and order for a healthy life: realises that they need to wash their hands after play and before eating; turns off the water after using it.

TADB.3 · Analysing a story they hear or watch: identifies the parts of events and retells what they heard in the order it happened (play → hand washing → watermelon; water → soap → rubbing → rinsing → towel).
E1.2 Independence (disposition): like Ela, takes action for their own cleanliness without waiting for a grown-up's reminder and does the steps themselves.
SDB3.3 Responsible Decision-Making: even though hungry, stops, looks at their hands, thinks about the consequence and chooses to wash their hands first.
D18 Cleanliness: discovers that clean hands feel 'so fresh'; takes ownership of cleanliness like a game.
once: Look at the cover together: “What do you think bubbly hands are like? What sound do bubbles make?”
Look at the child's hands together: “Where have our hands touched today?” Listen to the answers without correcting them.
Play the sounds from the story beforehand: splat (mud), grumble grumble (tummy), splish splash (water), bubbles bubbles (soap), click (tap).
sirasi: On page 1, touch the mud and make the “Splat!” sound together; point to the mud on Ela's hands.
For the prediction on page 3, accept both options: “They need both! But which one first?”
On page 4, the child touches the tap, the soap and Ela in order; rub your own hands together in the air and count to five together.
On page 5, touch Ela (rinse), the tap (Click! turn off) and Paws (towel) in order; join in with “Splish splash… Click! Pat pat!”
sonra: In the ordering game at the end of the story, put the three pictures in order; then let the child tell the events in their own words.
Ask “Why did Ela stop? What would have happened if she hadn't?”; be open to different answers.
When do we wash our hands? Make a picture list together: after play, before eating, after the toilet, after stroking our pet.

sinif.materyal: 5 picture sequence cards (tap, soap, bubbly hands, rinsing, towel), liquid soap, personal towels or paper towels, tape
adim: In the circle, show the cards mixed up; ask “What do we do first?” and let the children put the cards in order.

Go to the sink in small groups. Each child washes their hands looking at the cards; while rubbing, say the rhyme “Splish splash water, bubbly bubbly soap, rub rub rub, hands so fresh!” twice (about 20 seconds).
Make turning off the tap into a game with the “Click!” sound: don't let the water run for nothing.
Hang the cards next to the sink from left to right; let them be a guide all day.
In the review circle, ask: “Did you smell your hands? How do they smell?” Observe whether they can put the steps in order in their own words.

evSoru: Why didn't Ela eat the watermelon straight away?
When you wash your hands, what do you do first, and what do you do next?
How do you think Paws's paws get cleaned?

evEtk.d: For one week, before meals, take turns so that someone in the family is the “hand-washing captain.” The captain reminds everyone of the steps with “First water, then soap!”, starts the rhyme and turns off the water. After washing, smell each other's hands: “So fresh!”

guide.aileNotu: Today we read “Bubbly Hands.” After playing in the garden with her dog Paws, Ela runs to the watermelon; but she stops all by herself and washes her hands first. At home, do the hand-washing steps (water, soap, rubbing, rinsing, towel) together in order and make turning off the water into a game. When reminding, ask instead of warning: “What do you think our hands need now?” Leaving the decision to the child strengthens their sense of responsibility.
